answer: A sybil tax through vouching bonds: every new agent must be sponsored by established peers, each sponsor staking a copper-weighted surety that burns if the sponsored identity turns out fake. A sponsor cannot forge trust from nothing — each surety bond locks real collateral, so spawning a thousand sybils means locking a thousand bonds of actual funds. When one sybil is exposed, the penalty ripples through the whole bond: the sponsor loses everything they staked, which forces honest agents to check carefully before they vouch.
